title: Building a Commander deck
summary: The shape a 100-card deck wants, the five jobs every card can do, synergy as points of contact, ways to win, and what really sets a deck's bracket.

checklist.label: I know the shape a 100-card deck wants
I can name a card's job: ramp, draw, answer, wipe or finisher
I know what points of contact are
I know what actually sets a deck's bracket

steps.title: The shape of a 100-card deck
steps.body:
A Commander deck is 100 cards, and most good ones share a shape:

- **37 or 38 lands**
- **10 or 11 [[ramp]]** cards (extra mana)
- **12 or more [[card-advantage]]** cards (extra cards)
- **About 10 answers**: [[removal]] spells, plus **2 to 4 [[board-wipe|board wipes]]**
- Only **3 or 4 cards that cost 6 or more**

That leaves about 30 slots for the cards that make the deck yours. Build the skeleton first, then add the fun.

visual.altText: A 100-card deck split into lands, ramp, card draw, answers and the rest.

check.question: A deck has 31 lands and 40 creatures. What's the first thing to fix?

options.text: Add lands: 31 is too few for 100 cards

check.hint: Most Commander decks run 37 or 38 lands.

steps.title: Every card has a job
steps.body:
Read the rules text, not the name, and ask what job a card does:

- **[[ramp|Ramp]]**: makes extra mana. "Add {G}", "search your library for a basic land".
- **[[card-advantage|Card advantage]]**: draws extra cards. Draw-then-discard doesn't count.
- **[[removal|Removal]]**: "destroy target", "exile target", "counter target spell".
- **[[board-wipe|Board wipe]]**: "destroy all creatures".
- **[[finisher|Finisher]]**: ends the game from a normal board, not a dream one.

A card can do two jobs at once. Those are the best ones.

visual.altText: Five job labels with the rules text that signals each.

check.question: "When this creature enters, search your library for a basic land card and put it onto the battlefield tapped. When it dies, draw a card." Which jobs?
check.hint: Count every job the text does.

steps.title: Synergy: points of contact
steps.body:
A deck is a machine, not a pile of good cards. Write down what your commander cares about: its creature types, its triggers ("whenever a land enters"), its keywords.

For every other card, count how many of those things it touches. That number is its **points of contact**, its [[synergy]].

- **2 or 3 points**: it belongs.
- **1 point**: a passenger. Swap it for something denser.
- **0 points**: cut it, however strong it looks alone.

Lands, ramp and answers are exempt: every deck needs them.

visual.altText: A commander's three interests, and cards touching three, one and zero of them.

check.question: Your commander says "Whenever a land you control enters, you gain 1 life and draw a card." Which card has the most points of contact?

options.text: A spell that puts two lands onto the battlefield

check.hint: Two lands entering means two triggers.

steps.title: Ways to win
steps.body:
Every deck needs **3 or 4 real ways to close a game**. Common shapes:

- **Combat**: big or evasive creatures, trample, double damage.
- **Voltron**: one huge creature and 21 [[commander-damage|commander damage]].
- **Go wide**: many tokens and an anthem.
- **Drain**: creatures dying or life gained costs each opponent life.
- **Big mana**: a huge X spell.

A card that only helps when you are already winning is not a win condition.

visual.altText: Five ways a Commander deck closes a game.

check.question: Which of these counts as a way to win?

options.text: A 6/6 flying creature your deck can cast most games
A spell that doubles your life when you're already at 80

check.hint: It has to close from a normal board.

steps.title: What really sets the bracket
steps.body:
A [[bracket]] is not a feeling. Wizards' rules set a floor from a few hard signals:

- **[[game-changer|Game Changers]]**: 1 to 3 of them makes a deck at least **Bracket 3**; 4 or more, **Bracket 4**.
- A cheap **two-card infinite combo** that wins early: Bracket 4.
- **Mass land destruction** or **chained extra turns**: Bracket 4.

A tuned deck with none of these is **Bracket 2**, however good it is. Being well built does not raise the bracket; only those signals do.

visual.altText: The signals that raise a deck's bracket floor.

check.question: A perfectly tuned deck has 0 Game Changers, no combos, no land destruction and no extra turns. Which bracket is it?
check.hint: Only the signals raise the floor.

steps.title: Stars are not power
steps.body:
When people rate a deck out of five stars, the stars say **how good it is within its bracket**. The bracket says **how powerful it is**. A two-star Bracket 4 deck beats a five-star Bracket 2 deck.

An honest rating is strict: a deck that simply works, with the right shape and a plan, is **three stars**. Four or five must be earned by matching proven decklists.

The Deck doctor on the Commander screen checks any list this way.

visual.altText: Stars within a bracket versus the bracket itself.

check.question: Which deck is more powerful: a five-star Bracket 2 deck or a two-star Bracket 4 deck?
check.hint: The bracket is the power tier.
